title: Recover the shifted line from preservation on the coefficient unit
statement: Let Λ be a commutative condensed ring, f : X → S a morphism of schemes with S quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and L an internal Λ_X-module. Use the ordinary unbounded derived module categories and finite-constant-model Dbc of [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. If Lf* followed by tensor with single(L) and shift by two preserves the localizing closures of Dbc, then single(L)[2] belongs to Loc(Dbc(X,Λ)). The functor is exactly the twist of [def-sfb-tate-twisted-projection-comparison], and the closure is [sk-def-localizing-closure]. No finite-presentation assumption on L is added.

source.place: Well-definedness (3), proof step 11; coefficient-unit argument in step 5

proof.text: Give the regular coefficient module its rank-one finite presentation and the zero module its zero presentation. On the one-stratum partition, the identity cover and monoidal inverse-image unit comparisons identify these modules with their finite scalar models. The degree-zero coefficient unit has that regular module as H^0 and zero other cohomology; it is bounded and constructible. The existing constructibility well-definedness theorem transports the models along the homology comparison isomorphisms.

The assumed preservation applies to this generator of Loc(Dbc(S)). Exact pullback commutes with single, and its monoidal unit comparison identifies the pullback of the coefficient unit with the coefficient unit on X. The derived single/unit comparison and the tensor left unitor therefore identify its tensor with single(L) with single(L). Shift this isomorphism by two. Repleteness in the defining intersection for the localizing closure transports membership to single(L)[2]. This works also for empty schemes and for L=0.
